chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man whose wife had divorced him by mutual agreement (khula'); is it permissible for him to propose to her sister before her waiting period expires? He said: When her bond of marriage is freed and there is no reversion (raj'a) for him, then it is permissible for him to propose to her sister.

He said: And he was asked about a man who had two slave-sister concubines, so he slept with one of them, then he slept with the other. He said: When he slept with the second, the first becomes prohibited to him until the second dies.

I said: What is your view if he sells her? He said: If he sells her due to a need and no thought of the second comes to his mind, then I see no problem with that; and if he sells her in order to return to the first, then no.

key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Reversion (right to take back wife during iddah)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a man to marry two sisters or hold two slave sisters simultaneously in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between khula' (mutual divorce) and talaq (unilateral divorce) regarding the prohibition of marrying two sisters simultaneously. For free women, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits proposing to the sister before the waiting period ends if the husband has no right of reversion (raj'a), whereas for slave concubines, sexual intimacy with the second permanently prohibits the first until her death or sale, unless the sale is for a general need rather than specifically to free the first. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that the prohibition for slaves is stricter and more permanent than for free women, reflecting the unique status of concubinage in classical fiqh.
